subject: Culture
title: Communion and Shared Bread
description: A 60-second lesson on Communion and Shared Bread.

hook.text: Christians eat bread and drink wine as the body and blood of Christ. A meal becomes a sacrament.

buildup.text: Shared bread appears across religions. Breaking bread together signals trust and spiritual unity.

discovery.text: The word 'companion' comes from Latin: com (with) + panis (bread). A companion is who you eat with.

twist.text: Sikh langars feed thousands of strangers for free daily. The shared meal erases caste and wealth.

climax.text: A shared meal isn't just nutrition. Across faiths, it's the purest form of human communion.

quiz.question: What does the Latin root of 'companion' literally mean?
